question.stem:
A new company policy requires IAM users to change their passwords’ minimum length to 12 characters. After a random inspection, you found out that there are still employees who do not follow the policy.
How can you automatically check and evaluate whether the current password policy for an account complies with the company password policy?
options: Create a CloudTrail trail. Filter the result by setting the attribute to “Event Name” and lookup value to “ChangePassword”. This easily gives you the list of users who have made changes to their passwords.
Configure AWS Config to trigger an evaluation that will check the compliance for a user’s password periodically.

Create a rule in the Amazon CloudWatch event. Build an event pattern to match events on IAM. Set the event name to “ChangePassword” in the event pattern. Configure SNS to send notifications to you whenever a user has made changes to his password.
Create a Scheduled Lambda Function that will run a custom script to check compliance against changes made to the passwords periodically.
question.explanation: AWS Config continuously evaluates resource configuration against rules. The managed rule iam-password-policy checks whether the account password policy meets requirements such as minimum length (12) and reports compliant or non-compliant with no code to write. CloudTrail and CloudWatch/EventBridge events on ChangePassword only show that a user changed a password, they do not tell whether it meets the policy length. A scheduled Lambda would need a custom script to write and maintain, which is not the automatic managed check the question asks for.

concept: AWS Config managed rule iam-password-policy checks the account password policy for compliance
tests: Knowing that AWS Config (managed rule iam-password-policy) evaluates compliance with a password policy, while CloudTrail and EventBridge only record ChangePassword events.
expected: AWS Config managed rule iam-password-policy with parameters (MinimumPasswordLength 12, etc.), periodic or change-triggered evaluation, compliance shown per account. Triggers: 'automatically check and evaluate', 'complies with the policy', 'password policy'.
why_not: CloudTrail only logs the ChangePassword API call (who and when), it never evaluates the password against a policy. An EventBridge rule on ChangePassword just sends a notification for each change with no compliance check. A scheduled Lambda with a custom script could work but is custom code to maintain, while a managed Config rule exists.
